source.version: IZA Discussion Paper No. 17302, September 2024 (working paper). Locators below give the PDF page and the printed page; PDF page = printed page + 2.
source.title_on_document: Creative and Strategic Capabilities of Generative AI: Evidence from Large-Scale Experiments

supplement.where: Not located; the text says only 'available in the supplementary materials' (PDF p. 12, printed p. 10). The appendix (Tables 13-16, Figures 6-8) is in this PDF.
supplement.holds: Comprehensive experimental instructions and 'additional data supporting our conclusions'. All regression tables used here (Tables 2, 5, 14, 15, 16) are in the main PDF; no participant-level SDs or arm means are reported anywhere in the PDF.

paper_design_summary: Writers recruited on Prolific (1250 US adults) were randomly assigned to HumanBaseline (write alone), HumanAgainstAI (write alone, told they compete with AI texts for the top-10% bonus), or HumanPlusAI (allowed to use Bard, ChatGPT-3.5 or ChatGPT-4) and wrote one creative text of up to 1000 characters in 10 minutes. ChatGPT-4 (224) and Bard (216) texts were generated with the same prompts. 3336 separate online raters (in three rater-information groups) and five RAs rated each text 0-10 on creativity, originality, surprise and usefulness; idea diversity per source was measured with sBERT embeddings and hierarchical clustering.

studies.label: Writer experiment: HumanPlusAI vs HumanBaseline (and HumanAgainstAI)

assignment.what_was_assigned: Writing condition: HumanBaseline (no AI), HumanAgainstAI (no AI, competition with AI texts announced), HumanPlusAI (access to Bard or ChatGPT-3.5/4, tool chosen by participant)
assignment.quote: Human participants were randomly assigned to one of three treatments
assignment.prereg_locator: PDF p. 3, title footnote: 'pre-registered on AEA Registry, AEARCTR-0011584'

arms.name: HumanBaseline
arms.description: Wrote creative text alone; top 10% most creative humans receive a 5 GBP bonus.

arms.name: HumanPlusAI
arms.description: Had the choice to use Bard or ChatGPT (3.5 or 4); declared the tool before writing. Declared use: Bard 39, ChatGPT-3.5 184, ChatGPT-4 86 (footnote 4). Prolific description requested participants with an OpenAI or Bard account.

arms.name: HumanAgainstAI
arms.description: Wrote alone, told entries compete with AI-produced texts for the top-10% bonus. Not an AI-assistance arm.

participants.exclusions: Arm counts 688/253/309 (sum 1250) are the counts the paper reports and uses (Table 1). Footnote 3 says 702, 304 and 315 complete responses were received against pre-registered targets of 700, 300, 300; the paper does not explain the gap (14, 51, 6) between complete responses and analyzed counts. No count at assignment is given.
participants.who: US adults recruited on Prolific, described as a representative population of US adults; Table 1: about 48-50 percent male, mean age about 44.
participants.quote: We recruited 1250 participants from the U.S. through the Prolific platform to participate in a divergent (unconstrained) creative task
participants.locator: PDF p. 9 (printed p. 7), Section 2.1.1 and footnote 3; PDF p. 13 (printed p. 11), Table 1

ai_tool.name_model: Bard, ChatGPT-3.5, ChatGPT-4 (participant's own account and choice)
ai_tool.how_used: HumanPlusAI participants could use their chosen chatbot to help produce the text; intro says they 'were instructed to use them' (PDF p. 5), Section 2.1.1 says they 'had the choice to utilize' it (PDF p. 10). All 309 declared a tool (footnote 4).

task.description: Write a text of up to 1000 characters that is as creative as possible, choosing between 'If you had the talent to invent things just by thinking of them, what would you create?' and 'Imagine and describe a town, city, or society in the future.' Top 10% (rated by others) earned a 5 GBP bonus.
task.duration: Maximum 10 minutes; mean time 5.98 min (Baseline), 5.55 (HumanPlusAI), 6.67 (HumanAgainstAI), Table 1

outcomes.name: Overall creativity rating by online raters (0-10)
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Prolific raters scored 20 random texts each, 0-10, 'In general, how creative was this response?'; each text rated at least 10 times; OLS with rater fixed effects, SE clustered by response (one response per writer). Robustness: Table 2 cols 2-8 (prompt, demographic and full controls; gender splits) and Table 15 (writers with writing time > 180 s): HumanPlusAI 0.458*** (0.054).

contrasts.reported: Table 2 col (1): HumanPlusAI 0.500*** (0.052); col (5) all controls: 0.474*** (0.052); Observations 63,812 (ratings, all sources). Gender split col (6): Female 0.565*** (0.065), Male 0.435*** (0.073). Table 3 mean ratings for HumanPlusAI texts by tool: Bard 5.57 (39 texts), ChatGPT-3.5 5.93 (184), ChatGPT-4 5.84 (86); no HumanBaseline mean printed. Figure 1 shows rating distributions.

outcomes.name: Ratio of unique ideas across a condition's texts (idea diversity)
outcomes.question: across_people
outcomes.measure_detail: Texts embedded with Sentence-BERT; pairwise cosine distances within each source; Ward hierarchical clustering; clusters below a global distance threshold (0.5 or 1) count as one idea; ratio = unique ideas / number of texts. Three samples: all texts, top 100 texts within source, top 10 percent pooled. Figures 6-8 show all thresholds 0-2.

contrasts.reported: Table 7, ratio of unique ideas, threshold (0.5)/(1): ALL: HumanAndAI 29.9% / 7.3% vs HumanBaseline 30.2% / 6.7%; Top 100: 38.0% / 6.0% vs 52.0% / 10.0%; Top 10%: 50.0% / 12.5% vs 64.5% / 9.7%. HumanAgainstAI ALL 35.9% / 6.9%. No test reported.
contrasts.locator: PDF p. 23 (printed p. 21), Table 7; PDF pp. 39-40 (printed pp. 37-38), Figures 6-8

diversity_detail.metric: Ratio of unique ideas (number of clusters below a global cosine-distance threshold of 0.5 or 1, divided by number of texts)
diversity_detail.computed_over: All texts within each source (condition); also top 100 texts within source and top 10 percent of texts pooled across sources
diversity_detail.uncertainty: None reported (descriptive ratios, no test or interval)
diversity_detail.notes: Higher ratio = more diverse. Not a similarity measure, so no sign reversal. Top-10% sample has small and unequal text counts per source.

assignment.what_was_assigned: Rater information condition: original texts, grammar-corrected human texts, or grammar-corrected texts with disclosure that some are AI-generated plus an incentivized source guess
assignment.quote: The raters were divided into three treatment groups

arms.name: BaselineRaters
arms.description: Rated 20 original texts (human or AI), not told about AI.

arms.name: CorrectedRaters
arms.description: Rated 20 texts with human texts grammar-corrected by ChatGPT.

arms.name: AIRaters
arms.description: As CorrectedRaters, told some texts are AI-generated and asked to guess the source.

participants.exclusions: Section 2.1.2 gives 3336 raters (1100, 1090, 1146). Footnote 6 says 3,424 raters were hired; 81 who gave fewer than 10 ratings and the second participation of 18 repeat raters were excluded. Which count is the analyzed count is not stated explicitly.
participants.who: New Prolific participants, paid 2 GBP each
participants.country: United States (implied by recruitment pool; not stated for raters)
participants.quote: Subsequently, 3336 new participants were recruited to evaluate the text produced by humans and AI
participants.locator: PDF p. 10 (printed p. 8), Section 2.1.2; PDF p. 11 (printed p. 9), footnote 6

ai_tool.how_used: No AI assistance; raters judged others' texts.

task.description: Rate 20 texts 0-10 on creativity, originality, surprise and usefulness; AIRaters also guessed the source.

eligibility.reason: S1 states that 1250 Prolific writers were randomly assigned to HumanBaseline, HumanAgainstAI or HumanPlusAI (PDF p. 9); the AI contrast analyzes 309 HumanPlusAI vs 688 HumanBaseline people; outcomes are creativity, originality, surprise and usefulness of the written text rated by online raters and RAs (Tables 2, 5, 14, 16). Caveat for criterion 1: the HumanPlusAI Prolific description requested people with an OpenAI or Bard account (PDF p. 10) and arm sizes follow fixed targets, so the arms may not have been drawn from one pool. S2 adds ai_vs_human context; S3 is a perception experiment out of scope.

one_line_finding: Writers with access to a chatbot (HumanPlusAI, n = 309) received higher online creativity ratings than HumanBaseline writers (n = 688), 0.500 points on a 0-10 scale (SE 0.052, Table 2, PDF p. 15), while ChatGPT-4 alone scored 1.879 (SE 0.039) above HumanBaseline.
open_questions: Was assignment to HumanPlusAI drawn from the same recruitment pool? The Prolific description for that arm requested existing OpenAI or Bard account holders (PDF p. 10), and the pre-registered arm targets were 700/300/300 (footnote 3).
Why do analyzed counts (688/253/309) differ from complete responses (702/304/315, footnote 3)? No exclusion rule is stated.

RA ratings conflict: HumanPlusAI is higher on overall creativity (Table 5, 0.142) but lower on originality (-0.416) and surprise (-0.338) in Table 16; Table 16 notes mention online raters. Worth checking whether Table 16 is correctly labelled.
Rater-experiment assignment (S3) is not stated as random, and its analyzed count (3336 vs 3,424 hired) is not stated explicitly.
No participant-level means or SDs are printed; standard errors are clustered by response, which equals the writer for human texts (one text per writer).
notes: The strategic task (24 rounds of rock-paper-scissors against a pre-set opponent, Balanced vs Unbalanced, played by the same writers and by ChatGPT-4 in 200 chats; Tables 11-12, Figure 5) is not a creativity outcome and is not coded as a study. Also not coded: Table 6 correlates of creativity with writer characteristics, Tables 8-10 rater-treatment effects, source guesses and identification rates (perception outcomes), and a 2-month follow-up survey with self-reported creativity (79.6 percent response rate). The HumanAgainstAI arm is a competition-framing arm without AI assistance; its contrasts are recorded with comparison_type 'other' under S1-O1 and in the reported strings of other outcomes. Holzner et al. (2025) meta-analysis lists this paper (per candidate record, not verified here).
